It is also used in dishes like Punjabi black dal and in some South Indian preparations. Soak overnight and cook patiently for the best texture. Served with naan, rice or rotis, it makes a comforting meal for family dinners and celebrations. For those who want to cook authentic dal makhani or other slow-cooked lentil dishes at home, it is a staple worth stocking.

name: RAJDHANI URAD DAL DHULI 500G
description:
URAD DAL DHULI: 
Dhuli urad dal is the skinned, split black gram that forms the base of many Indian favourites. Soak and grind it with rice for idli and dosa batter, or use it in medu vada, dahi vada, dal makhani and the stuffing for kachori. It also appears in tadkas and papad-making. The dal ferments well and gives a soft, fluffy texture in batters. For South Indian breakfasts, North Indian festive dishes and traditional home cooking, it is a pantry essential that serves many recipes.

name: RAJDHANI DESI KALA CHANA 500G
description:
VEDAKA DESI KALA CHANA: 
Desi kala chana are small, dark chickpeas with an earthy flavour and firm bite. Soak and boil them for kala chana curry, ghugni, sundal, chaat, salads and the traditional Navratri prasad of sooji halwa, puri and chana. They also feature in sprouts and snack bowls. Their hearty texture holds well in gravies and stir-fries. For households that enjoy traditional vegetarian dishes, festive offerings and street-style snacks, they are a versatile, familiar pantry ingredient.

name: RAJDHANI MOONG DAL SABUT WHOLE 500G
description:
MOONG DAL SABUT (WHOLE): 
Whole moong, with its green skin intact, has an earthy flavour and a hearty bite that sets it apart from the split, skinned variety. Soak and cook it for dal tadka, curries, khichdi and soups, or sprout it for salads and chaat. It is also used in traditional Rajasthani and Gujarati dishes, such as moong ki sabzi and spiced stews. The whole beans keep their shape while becoming tender, which gives dishes more texture. For households that enjoy rustic, home-style Indian cooking and like to vary their daily dal, it provides a flexible ingredient that works for simple lunches, sprouts and festive recipes.

name: RAJDHANI ARHAR TOOR DAL 500G
description:
ARHAR TOOR DAL: 
Arhar, or toor dal, is a staple in Indian homes, forming the base of everyday dal and South Indian sambar. Pressure-cook it until soft, then temper with cumin, garlic, curry leaves or mustard seeds for a comforting bowl. It features in Gujarati dal, dal fry, rasam and vegetable-lentil stews. Its full, earthy taste pairs well with rice, rotis and ghee. For households that cook dal daily, it offers a dependable, familiar base for countless regional recipes, from simple weeknight meals to festive spreads.

name: RAJDHANI MOONG DAL DHULI 500G
description:
MOONG DAL DHULI: 
Dhuli moong dal is skinned and split yellow moong, known for its mild taste and soft, quick-cooking texture. Use it for moong dal tadka, khichdi, chilla, halwa and light soups. It blends easily with ghee, cumin, ginger and asafoetida for simple comforting meals. It is also a popular choice for fasting-day recipes and for dishes prepared when something gentle on the palate is wanted. Because it cooks fast and needs minimal soaking, it suits daily cooking in busy homes, offering a versatile base for both everyday and festive recipes.

name: RAJDHANI CHANA DAL 500G
description:
CHANA DAL: 
Split Bengal gram, known as chana dal, has a nutty taste and firm texture that holds up well in cooking. Soak and pressure-cook it for dal tadka, lauki chana dal, dhaba-style dal or the filling in puran poli and stuffed parathas. It also goes into chutneys, vadas, khichdi and South Indian sundal. Its slightly sweet, earthy flavour pairs well with ghee, cumin and garlic tempering. For everyday Indian cooking where lentils form the heart of the meal, it is a versatile staple suited to both festive recipes and simple lunches.

name: RAJDHANI CHOLE KABULI CHANA 500G
description:
CHOLE KABULI CHANA: 
Kabuli chana, or white chickpeas, are firm, creamy legumes that star in chole, one of North India's most popular dishes. Soak overnight and pressure-cook until tender, then simmer in a spiced onion-tomato gravy for chole bhature or chole kulche. They also work in chana chaat, hummus-style dips, salads, pulao and soups. Their mild, nutty taste and satisfying bite make them versatile. For weekend meals, party menus and street-food-style snacks, a pack of kabuli chana is a useful staple for any Indian pantry.

name: COCONAD COCONUT MILK POWDER 1KG
description:
COCONUT MILK POWDER: 
Coconut milk powder offers the creamy taste of coconut milk in a dry, easy-to-store form. Mix it with warm water as directed to make coconut milk whenever you need it, then use it in curries, stews, kurma, rice dishes, desserts and beverages. It can also be added to sweets, milkshakes, tea and coffee for a coconut note. The powder keeps well on the shelf, which is useful for households that do not cook with coconut milk every day. For cooks who want authentic coastal flavours with flexible quantities and simple storage, it is a practical alternative to cans and fresh coconut.

name: COCONAD COCONUT MILK 400ML
description:
COCONUT MILK: 
Coconut milk is central to the cooking of Kerala, Karnataka, Goa and the coastal belt, giving curries, stews and desserts a rich, creamy body. Stir it into fish curry, vegetable stew, kurma, appam accompaniments or rice dishes to add a smooth, mellow sweetness that balances spice. It also works in payasam, kheer, puddings and beverages. Having it ready saves the effort of grating, grinding and straining fresh coconut, which is helpful on busy days. Add it towards the end of cooking over gentle heat for the best texture. For cooks who want authentic South Indian and coastal flavours and a creamy finish in curries and sweets, it is a convenient kitchen staple.

name: COCONAD COCONUT WATER 200ML
description:
COCONUT WATER: 
Coconut water is a familiar refreshment in coastal India and across the tropics, with a light, mildly sweet taste that suits hot weather. Serve it chilled on its own, or use it as a base for summer coolers, fruit drinks and smoothies. It is a popular drink after a day outdoors or alongside a light meal. This packaged version offers the taste of the tender coconut without having to crack one open, making it easy to keep in the fridge, carry on trips or offer to guests. For people who enjoy the gentle, natural sweetness of coconut water in a convenient pack, it is a handy everyday choice.

name: COCONAD DECICATED COCONUT POWDER 40G
description:
DECICATED COCONUT POWDER: 
Desiccated coconut is dried, finely shredded coconut with a mild, sweet flavour and a pleasing, slightly chewy texture. Use it in Indian sweets such as coconut ladoo, barfi, halwa and modak, or sprinkle it over cakes, cookies, puddings and fruit salads. It also works in chutneys, curries, stuffed parathas and masala pastes where fresh coconut is traditionally used. It saves the effort of breaking and grating coconuts, and keeps well on the shelf. For festive cooking, baking and everyday recipes that call for coconut, it is a convenient pantry staple, particularly for busy kitchens during Diwali, Ganesh Chaturthi and other celebrations.

name: DHARA SARSON TEL MUSTARD OIL BOTTLE 500ML
description:
SARSON TEL (MUSTARD OIL): 
Mustard oil is a traditional cooking oil in many Indian regions, valued for its sharp aroma and pungent flavour. Heat it until it smokes lightly before using, then use it for tadkas, fish curry, sabzis, parathas and pickles. It is closely linked with Bengali, Punjabi, Bihari and Kashmiri cuisines, where its taste is central to recipes. It also dresses salads and jhal muri. For cooks who want authentic regional flavour in traditional dishes, it offers a familiar aroma that is hard to replicate with milder oils.

name: WAI WAI CHICKEN MASALA NOODLE 70G
description:
CHICKEN FLAVOR MASALA NOODLE: 
Instant noodles have become a popular snack across India and neighbouring regions, and this chicken masala variety comes with a savoury, spiced flavour. Cook the noodles in boiling water, stir in the seasoning, and enjoy as a quick meal or snack within minutes. Many people add chopped onions, tomatoes, green chillies, vegetables or an egg for extra taste and texture. Some also eat the noodles dry, crushed with the masala, as a crunchy street-style snack. It suits after-school hunger, late-evening cravings, hostel cooking and travel. For anyone who wants a fast, flavourful bowl with a familiar masala taste and the freedom to customise toppings, it provides a convenient, easy-to-prepare option for everyday snacking.

name: WAI WAI VEG MASALA NOODLE 70G
description:
VEG MASALA NOODLE: 
Instant noodles are popular quick snacks across India and neighbouring regions, and this veg masala version brings a savoury, spiced flavour. Many people add chopped onions, tomatoes, green chillies, carrots, peas or an egg for extra taste and texture. Some enjoy the noodles dry, crushed with the masala, as a crunchy street-style snack. For those who want a fast, flavourful bowl with a familiar masala taste and room for customisation, it is a convenient option.

name: PUSHP JEERA CUMIN SEEDS WHOLE 500G
description:
PUSHP JEERA CUMIN SEEDS WHOLE: 
Whole cumin seeds are the starting point of many Indian tadkas. Add them to hot ghee or oil until they crackle, releasing a warm, earthy aroma that flavours dals, sabzis, rice and raita. They are used in jeera rice, aloo jeera, kadhi, khichdi and buttermilk. They can also be dry-roasted and ground for chaat masala and raita topping. Buying whole seeds lets you control texture and freshness, and a small spoonful transforms a plain dish into something fragrant. A pantry basic for everyday Indian cooking.

name: GANPATI GULAB JAL ROSE WATER 250G
description:
GULAB JAL (ROSE WATER): 
Gulab jal, or rose water, carries a delicate floral fragrance that has long been part of Indian kitchens, rituals and festivals. Add a few drops to kheer, phirni, gulab jamun syrup, halwa, lassi, falooda, sherbets and biryani to give them a soft, perfumed aroma. It is a familiar ingredient in Mughlai and North Indian sweets, where the rose note signals a special occasion. Rose water is also used in religious offerings and festive preparations in many homes. A little goes a long way, so a bottle lasts across many recipes. For cooks who like to give desserts and drinks a traditional fragrance, it is a useful pantry addition for celebrations and everyday cooking alike.

name: GANPATI KEWRA WATER 250G
description:
KEWRA WATER: 
Kewra water is a fragrant essence distilled from the flowers of the screwpine, widely used in North Indian and Mughlai cooking for its sweet, floral aroma. Add a few drops to biryani, pulao, kheer, phirni, gulab jamun, rabri, sherbets and lassi to give them a distinctive, perfumed note that signals a special occasion. In many households, it is a classic ingredient for festive meals, particularly during Eid, Diwali and weddings. A small amount is enough, so a bottle lasts across many recipes. For cooks who want to add a traditional, fragrant finish to rice dishes and desserts, it is a useful pantry addition that carries the heritage of royal kitchens.

name: RAJDHANI BESAN GRAM FLOUR 500G
description:
BESAN (GRAM FLOUR): 
Besan is a fine flour made from chana dal, and it is used across Indian kitchens for both savoury and sweet recipes. Whisk it into batter for pakoras, bhajiyas and kadhi, or roast it in ghee for besan ladoo and halwa. It also makes chilla, dhokla, khandvi and sev. Its nutty aroma and binding quality make it versatile, and it works as a coating for fried snacks. For monsoon pakoras, festive sweets and everyday breakfasts, it is a useful pantry staple.

name: RAJDHANI SATTU FLOUR 500G
description:
SATTU FLOUR: 
Sattu is a roasted gram flour with deep roots in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh. Use it to prepare traditional sattu paratha, litti chokha, and the cooling summer drink sattu sharbat with water, roasted cumin, salt or jaggery. It can also be mixed into laddoos and dough for stuffed breads. Its toasty aroma and earthy taste give regional dishes their authenticity. For those who want to cook traditional Bihari food or enjoy a simple homemade drink, it is a practical, heritage-rich ingredient.

name: RAJDHANI ROASTED CHANA SPICY 200G
description:
ROASTED CHANA SPICY: 
Roasted chana with a spicy seasoning is a crunchy, savoury snack that suits evening chai and quick bites between meals. The firm texture and nutty chickpea taste carry a lively masala kick, making it a favourite among those who like a little heat in their snacks. Enjoy it by the handful, pack it for travel, or toss it with chopped onions, tomatoes, coriander and lemon for a quick chaat. It also adds crunch to bhel and salads. For picnics, office breaks and casual gatherings, it provides a simple, traditional snack with a familiar Indian taste, easy to store and share, and suitable for those who prefer uncomplicated, spiced munching.

name: RAJDHANI GROUNDNUT PEANUT RAW 500G
description:
GROUNDNUT PEANUT RAW: 
Raw peanuts are a flexible Indian kitchen ingredient used in many regional dishes. Roast or fry them for chaat, poha, upma, chivda and masala peanuts, or grind them for chutneys, curries and sauces. They are a key ingredient in Maharashtrian and Gujarati recipes and are widely used in fasting-day preparations. Their nutty taste and crunch add contrast to soft dishes. Buying them raw lets you roast to your preferred crispness and use them across both snacks and cooking, making them a useful pantry item.

name: RAJDHANI MURMURA JHAL MURI PUFFED RICE 200G
description:
MURMURA (JHAL MURI) PUFFED RICE: 
Puffed rice, known as murmura or muri, is a light, airy ingredient that lies behind some of India's best-loved snacks. Toss it with chopped onions, tomatoes, green chilli, mustard oil, peanuts and a squeeze of lemon to prepare Kolkata-style jhal muri, or turn it into bhel, a roadside favourite across the country. It also works for chivda, sweet murmura ladoos and festive snack mixes. The crisp, neutral base soaks up masalas and chutneys while staying crunchy if served promptly. For evening tea, children's snack time or casual gatherings, it provides a simple foundation that lets you adjust spice, tang and toppings to your own taste. A handy pantry item for street-style snacking at home.

name: PINKOO PANI PURI GOLGAPPA FUCHKA 200G
description:
PANI PURI (GOLGAPPA) FUCHKA: 
Pani puri, called golgappa in the north and fuchka in the east, is among India's most loved street snacks, and these crisp hollow puris make it easy to recreate at home. Break a small opening in each puri, fill it with boiled potato, chickpeas and a little chutney, then dip it in chilled tangy pani made with mint, tamarind or lemon. The thin, crunchy shells shatter with each bite and soak up the flavourful water. They also work for dahi puri, sev puri and other chaat creations. For kitty parties, birthdays, festivals and rainy-evening gatherings, they let you serve a street-style favourite with your own fillings and spice levels, right at the dining table.

BHUT JOLOKIA HOT SAUCE
Bhut jolokia, also known as ghost pepper, is a chilli from India's Northeast, famous for its intense heat, and this 55g hot sauce brings that fire in a small bottle. Add a few drops to noodles, momos, eggs, pizzas, burgers, soups and curries, tasting as you go, since a little can be a lot. It also works as a dip for snacks or a marinade booster. For chilli lovers who enjoy testing their limits and adding bold heat to everyday meals, the compact bottle makes it easy to dose and store. Handle with care and keep away from eyes.

name: ZOFF CHICKEN MASALA 14G
description:
CHICKEN MASALA: 
This blend is made to season chicken curries, from a simple home-style gravy to a richer dhaba-style preparation. Add it to sautéed onions and tomatoes before the chicken goes in, and let the spices cook into the oil until fragrant. It also suits chicken fry, kadai chicken, dry-roasted chicken and pulao. The flavour is savoury and well-rounded, so the dish tastes complete without hunting through the spice rack. Served with steamed rice, rumali roti or hot chapatis, it fits family dinners, guest meals and weeknight cooking when you want a familiar, comforting chicken curry.

name: ZOFF MEAT MASALA 14G
description:
MEAT MASALA: 
A seasoning meant for mutton, lamb and other meat curries, it gives slow-cooked gravies a hearty, well-rounded depth. Add it after browning onions and ginger-garlic paste, then pressure-cook or simmer until the meat is tender. It suits Sunday mutton curry, keema, dry-fried masala meat and meat-based pulao. Because the flavour is warm and robust, it holds up well to long cooking and pairs well with rotis, naan, jeera rice or ghee-laced parathas. For cooks who want a dependable base for non-vegetarian dishes, it simplifies the spice step while leaving room to add extra chilli or garam masala to taste.

name: ZOFF KASURI METHI FENUGREEK LEAVES 25G
description:
KASURI METHI (FENUGREEK) LEAVES: 
Kasuri methi, dried fenugreek leaves, give North Indian gravies a distinctive, savoury aroma that many people associate with restaurant-style dishes. Crush a pinch between your palms and sprinkle over butter chicken, paneer makhani, dal makhani and kadhai dishes just before serving. It also flavours parathas, naan, thepla, pulao and masala omelettes. The leaves release their fragrance when warmed, so they are best added near the end of cooking. For home cooks who want their curries to smell and taste like their favourite restaurant versions, it is a small but impactful ingredient that supports a wide range of North Indian recipes.

KALA NAMAK (BLACK SALT) POWDER: 
Kala namak, or black salt, is a pinkish-grey rock salt with a distinctive savoury, tangy, slightly sulphurous aroma that Indian cooks prize. Sprinkle it on fruit chaat, boiled potatoes, cucumber, raita, buttermilk, jaljira and chaat for an unmistakable street-food taste. It is a key ingredient in chaat masala and in many homemade drink mixes. A little pinch is enough, as the flavour is strong. For those who enjoy the tangy-savoury side of Indian snacks and refreshments, it is a useful pantry item that brings depth to simple foods, from salads to lassi.

name: ZOFF KAALI MIRCH SABUT BLACK PEPPER WHOLE 100G
description:
KAALI MIRCH SABUT (BLACK PEPPER) WHOLE: 
Whole black peppercorns carry a sharp, aromatic heat that is quite different from chilli. Add them whole to tadkas, biryanis, pulaos, rasam and whole-spice blends, or crush fresh for use in soups, omelettes, salads, marinades and masala chai. LAUNG (LAVANG) CLOVE: 
Laung, or clove, is a strongly aromatic spice with a sweet, warming, slightly pungent taste. For cooks who like to use whole spices to build layered, fragrant flavour in rice dishes and gravies, it is an essential, traditional ingredient in the Indian pantry.

AJWAIN (CARROM SEEDS): 
Ajwain, also known as carom seeds, has a sharp, thyme-like aroma and a pungent bite that stands out in Indian cooking. CHOUNK TEJ PATTA (INDIAN BAY LEAF): 
Tej patta is the dried leaf used in Indian cooking to add a subtle, warm fragrance to dishes. description:
VEDAKA SAUNF (FENNEL) SEEDS: 
Fennel seeds have a sweet, cooling aroma and are used in Indian kitchens in both cooking and after-meal traditions. Chew a few after meals as mouth freshener, or add them to tadkas, pickles, panch phoron, meat curries and sweet dishes. They also flavour sherbets, thandai and chai. A light dry roast brings out the aroma. Their mildly sweet, licorice-like taste adds balance to savoury recipes and freshness to drinks. A small jar is a handy pantry item for both cooking and hospitality.

CHAKRA PHOOL (STAR ANISE): 
Chakra phool, or star anise, is a star-shaped spice with a sweet, licorice-like aroma. CORRIANDER WHOLE (DHANIYA SABUT):

Dry-roast them lightly and grind for fresh dhaniya powder, or add whole to tadkas, pickles, sambar powder, garam masala and curries. METHI (FENUGREEK SEEDS): 
Methi seeds are small, golden and distinctly aromatic, with a slightly bitter taste that becomes mellow when cooked. Add a few to hot oil for tadkas in sambar, rasam, pickles, dals and vegetable dishes, or use them in Bengali panch phoron and Gujarati methia masala. A small spoonful goes a long way, which makes a pack useful across many recipes. For cooks who enjoy authentic regional flavours, they are a traditional and versatile pantry spice.

name: ZOFF PANCHPHORAN WHOLE SPICES 100G
description:
PANCHPHORAN WHOLE SPICES: 
Panchphoran, meaning “five spices,” is a traditional whole-spice mix widely used in Bengali, Odia and Bihari cooking. It is usually a blend of cumin, mustard, fennel, fenugreek and nigella seeds, though the exact makeup varies by pack. Heat oil, add a spoonful until it crackles, then use it to temper dals, vegetable dishes, fish curries and chutneys. The mix gives food a distinctive, layered aroma that differs from common tadkas. For cooks who enjoy eastern Indian recipes and want an easy way to add authentic seasoning without measuring five separate spices, it is a convenient, characterful pantry item.

name: ZOFF WHITE SESAME SEEDS 100G
description:
WHITE SESAME SEEDS:

name: TASTY NB KANTHARI MANGO CHUTNEY 200G
description:
KANTHARI MANGO CHUTNEY: 
Kanthari refers to the fiery bird's-eye chilli popular in Kerala and South Indian cooking, and this mango chutney pairs that heat with the tang of mango. It offers a sweet-sour-spicy taste that brightens plain meals. Serve it with rice, curd rice, dosa, idli, chapati, parathas or as a sandwich spread for a flavourful lift. It also works as a side for snacks such as pakoras, cutlets and fried fish. A small portion is usually enough to add interest to simple food, making it a handy accompaniment for lunch boxes and travel meals. For those who enjoy bold, coastal-style condiments with a mix of tang and heat, it adds a distinctive regional note to everyday eating.

name: TASTY NB FRIED MASALA PRAWN JAR 50G
description:
FRIED MASALA PRAWN: 
A ready-to-eat prawn preparation seasoned with spices and fried, offering a savoury, seafood-rich bite. Enjoy it as a side with rice and dal, a starter with evening drinks or tea, or as a filling for wraps and rolls. The masala coating gives it a spicy, aromatic character that suits coastal Indian palates. It is convenient for guests, travel and quick meals when you want something non-vegetarian without cooking from scratch. For prawn lovers, it makes an easy, flavourful addition to the table.

name: MOTHERS RECP MANGO PICKLE JAR 900G
description:
MANGO PICKLE: 
Mango pickle is among India's most recognised achars, celebrated for its sour, spicy and oily tang. Serve it with parathas, puri-sabzi, dal-rice, curd rice, khichdi or simple rotis, where a small piece lifts the entire plate. Its sharp, aromatic taste has been a part of summer traditions in Indian homes for generations. It also works as a sandwich spread, wrap filling or side for snacks like thepla and dhokla. A jar on the table gives everyday meals a familiar, homely character that many families look for, especially when the main dish is mild.

name: MOTHERS RECP MIXED PICKLE JAR 900G
description:
MIXED PICKLE: 
Mixed pickle brings several tangy, spiced vegetables and fruits into one jar, so each bite tastes a little different. It is a traditional Indian condiment served alongside parathas, puris, thepla, dal-chawal, khichdi and curd rice. A small spoonful adds a sharp, savoury punch to plain meals and packed tiffins. It is also handy for travel, picnics and quick lunches where the main dish is simple. The oil-based tang and spice make it a lasting favourite on the Indian dining table, where pickle is regarded as an essential flavour partner rather than an extra.

name: WEL BAKED KHAKRA CHILLY GARLIC 1.4KG
description:
KHAKRA CHILLY GARLIC: 
Khakhra is a thin, crisp, roasted flatbread from Gujarat, and this baked version has a chilli and garlic seasoning for a savoury, lively flavour. The garlic gives it an aromatic edge while the chilli adds a gentle kick, making it a satisfying partner for morning chai or an evening snack. Enjoy it plain, with curd, chutney or pickle, or crush it over salads and chaat for texture. Its cracker-like crispness makes it easy to carry on trips, to the office or in school tiffins. For those who like a bit of spice in a light, crunchy snack with Indian regional roots, it provides a convenient, flavourful option that stores well.

name: GULAB PURE GUD JAGGERY 450G
description:
PURE GUD (JAGGERY): 
Gud, or jaggery, is a traditional Indian sweetener with a deep, caramel-like flavour. Use it in gur-wali chai, sweet dishes such as halwa, kheer, ladoos and chikki, or in sambar, dals and chutneys to balance sourness and spice. It is closely tied to festivals like Makar Sankranti, Lohri and Pongal, when sesame-jaggery sweets are made. A small piece after a meal is a familiar custom in many homes. Grate or crumble it for easy mixing into recipes. For households that like to cook with traditional sweeteners and want the earthy flavour of jaggery in their desserts and everyday dishes, it is a useful pantry staple.

name: THAKKAR CURRY PATTA LEAVES 50G
description:
CURRY PATTA (LEAVES): 
Curry leaves are indispensable in South Indian cooking and widely used across the country. Add them to hot oil with mustard seeds for a tadka and they sputter and release a fresh, slightly citrusy fragrance that defines sambar, rasam, poriyal, coconut chutney, upma and curd rice. They also flavour dals, kadhi, pickles and snacks like chivda. The leaves are usually eaten along with the dish or set aside on the plate. Having a pack on hand means you can build authentic South Indian tempering at any time. For cooks who want the signature aroma of regional cooking without relying on a fresh bunch, it is a handy pantry addition.

name: POOJA MITTI KA DIYA CLAY DIYA 10 PCS PACK 25G
description:
POOJA MITTI KA DIYA CLAY DIYA 10 PCS PACK: 
Mitti ke diye, traditional clay lamps, are central to Indian worship and festivals such as Diwali, Karthigai Deepam and Dev Deepawali. This pack of ten gives you enough for the prayer room, the doorstep and festive decorations. Fill with oil or ghee, add a cotton wick and light them for daily puja, evening aarti or celebrations. Clay lamps also suit rangoli decorations, housewarmings and festive gatherings, where their warm glow sets a welcoming mood. For households that like to keep their traditions alive with simple earthen diyas, a pack of ten is a practical, affordable festive essential.

name: POOJA COTTON BATTI LONG WIKS 20G
description:
POOJA COTTON BATTI LONG WIKS: 
Cotton batti, or wicks, are used in lighting diyas and lamps for daily worship, aarti and festivals across Indian homes. These long wicks suit larger lamps, deepams and lamp stands where a longer burn is wanted, and they can be cut to the size you need. Place a wick in oil or ghee, light the tip and enjoy a steady flame during puja. They are useful for temple lamps, festival decorations and daily rituals. For households that like to keep a supply of wicks ready for prayer and celebrations, a pack is a simple, essential pooja item.

name: POOJA COTTON BATTI ROUND WIKS 30G
description:
POOJA COTTON BATTI ROUND WIKS: 
Round cotton wicks, or gol batti, are small, rounded wicks commonly used in clay diyas and small lamps for daily puja, aarti and festive occasions. Place one in oil or ghee, light the tip and the diya burns with a gentle flame, creating a warm, devotional atmosphere. They suit daily prayers, Diwali decorations, temple visits and festive gatherings. For households that keep a regular puja routine and want a steady supply of wicks for their diyas, a pack of round batti is a simple, practical pooja essential that fits easily into the prayer corner.

name: POOJA INCENSE DHOOP STICKS 100G
description:
POOJA INCENSE DHOOP STICKS: 
Dhoop sticks are a traditional form of incense, burned during puja, aarti and quiet reflection in Indian homes. Light one end, let the flame settle, and the stick releases fragrant smoke that fills the room with a calming aroma. They suit morning and evening prayers, festivals, housewarmings and meditation. Place in a stand to catch ash and keep away from flammable items. For households that like to begin the day with a devotional fragrance or add atmosphere to puja rooms and festive occasions, a pack of dhoop sticks is a simple, practical pooja item.

description:
LAUNG (LAVANG) CLOVE: 
Laung, or clove, is a strongly aromatic spice with a sweet, warming, slightly pungent taste. Add one or two to hot oil at the start of tempering, or use in biryani, pulao, masala chai, garam masala and rich meat curries. It also features in kadha and homemade spice blends. A little goes a long way, so a small pack can last across many recipes. For cooks who like to use whole spices to build layered, fragrant flavour in rice dishes and gravies, it is an essential, traditional ingredient in the Indian pantry.

name: ZOFF JEERA CUMIN SEEDS WHOLE 27G
description:
PUSHP JEERA CUMIN SEEDS WHOLE: 
Whole cumin seeds are the starting point of many Indian tadkas. Add them to hot ghee or oil until they crackle, releasing a warm, earthy aroma that flavours dals, sabzis, rice and raita. They are used in jeera rice, aloo jeera, kadhi, khichdi and buttermilk. They can also be dry-roasted and ground for chaat masala and raita topping. Buying whole seeds lets you control texture and freshness, and a small spoonful transforms a plain dish into something fragrant. A pantry basic for everyday Indian cooking.

name: ZOFF RED CHILLI POWDER 45G
description:
KUTILAL RED CHILLI POWDER: 
Kutilal is a pungent, vibrant red chilli powder for cooks who like their food with noticeable heat and colour. It suits curries, dals, tadkas, pickles, chutneys, marinades and street-style snacks. Use it in generous pinches when preparing spicy gravies or when you want that classic red-oil look in the pan. A small amount is enough for mild dishes, while heavier-handed use gives dhaba-style curries their fire. It also seasons masala papad, fries and roasted peanuts. Households that enjoy bold, traditional Indian flavours often keep it as the everyday chilli powder in their spice box.
